---
title: "Install"
---

scjn needs Python 3.10 or newer.

```bash
pip install scjn
```

## What it depends on

| Package | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `requests` | every request to the SCOW API and to GitHub |
| `platformdirs` | picking the per-user cache directory |

## The cache directory

The release assets that `scjn download` and the `download_*_assets` functions
write, and that every reader looks at first, live in `scjn.cache.CACHE_DIR`:
an OS-appropriate per-user directory, `~/.cache/scjn` on Linux, overridable
with the environment variable `SCJN_CACHE_DIR`. It is the package's own and is
never shared with another package's cache.

## GitHub rate limit

Resolving a release's parts asks the GitHub API once, where an unauthenticated
address gets 60 requests an hour. When `GH_TOKEN` (or `GITHUB_TOKEN`) is set,
that request carries it as a bearer token; without one nothing changes. The
asset downloads themselves are outside that quota.

## Development install

```bash
pip install -e ".[test]"
pytest tests scripts/tests --ignore=tests/test_api_red.py --ignore=tests/test_release_red.py
```

The two ignored files make real network calls (the live SCOW API and the real
releases); CI runs them in their own `network` job.

## The scripts' dependency group

Three of the crawl scripts (`discover_federal_laws.py`,
`fetch_scjn_legislacion.py` and `recrawl_scjn_outline.py`) link laws to the DOF
and import `dofjson` and `nota2md` from PyPI, never the package itself:

```bash
uv sync --group scripts
# or
pip install dofjson nota2md
```

See [Crawl](crawl.qmd) for what each script does.
